chunks: Abu al-Hasan Musa ibn Ja'far عليه السلام was asked about a man whose hand had been cut off from the elbow: how should he perform wudu (ablution)? He said:
"He washes what remains of his upper arm."

And likewise it was narrated regarding the cutting of the leg. And when a woman performs wudu (ablution), she removes her head covering from the place of wiping her head in the Fajr and Maghrib prayers and wipes over it, and in the rest of the prayers it suffices her to insert her finger and wipe over her head without removing her head covering.

key_terms.رَأْسِهَا: her head, the place of wiping in wudu
key_terms.عَضُدِهِ: his upper arm, meaning the remaining part to be washed
key_terms.مَسْحِ: wiping, the prescribed act over the head in wudu
key_terms.يَغْسِلُ: washes as part of the prescribed ablution

ai.seo_question: How should a person with an amputated limb or a woman wearing a head covering perform wudu (ablution)?
ai.summary: This hadith gives legal rulings concerning wudu (ablution) in cases of physical limitation and practical dress concerns. It states that one who has lost a limb washes what remains, and it also outlines how a woman may manage wiping the head during wudu while wearing her head covering.
